title: The app sandbox: files, preferences, caches, and what the backup takes

videos.script:
An app on a phone has to keep working when the network is gone. {{tunnel}} In a tunnel, on a plane, in a basement with one bar. This course is about the data that makes that possible: what the app keeps on the device, and how it agrees with the server afterwards.

It starts with where the data lives. {{sandbox}} Every app gets a folder of its own, the sandbox. Android and iOS both split it into a few places, and the place a file goes decides whether the backup takes it. {{backup}} Today you measure that, and find a planner whose whole backup is skipped because of one PDF.

The example is a study planner. {{planner}} Courses, sessions, and the minutes in a week. You set up the folder it lives in, on your own computer.

And one thing is said now. {{boundary}} Everything you practise here runs in Node, on any computer. The Kotlin, Swift and React Native code is read, side by side, from each platform's documentation.
